correctness.rationale: For n>=4 any cross-part pair either dominates immediately (matched pair) or leaves exactly a_j and b_i, both forced by witnessed observed vertices with distinct index. A pure one-side set of s>=2 observes all opposite vertices, with n-s unobserved on its own side; each opposite vertex has exactly w or w-1 unseen neighbors. If w>=3 no force is possible, whereas w<=2 the stated explicit forces close all vertices. Singletons fail for n>=4; the empty set fails. This proves the iff classification, exact polynomial by disjoint selection families, and minimality by monotonicity. Finite exhaustive standalone verifier checked all 87,296 subsets for n=4..8, independent of the proposed eligibility rule; these computations corroborate, not prove, the quantified infinite theorem.
